What this Dallas pressure washing line is, and what it is not

If you searched for power washing in Dallas, this site gives you one number to call instead of a long list of companies to try.

Think of Dallas Power Washing Pro as a switchboard with a guidebook attached. It does no washing itself. An automated assistant answers (469) 649-7066 around the clock and asks what needs washing and where. If you need pressure or power washing, the call is transferred to an independent local company, which hears a short spoken summary before it picks up, so you do not have to start over. If no one answers, a message is taken and passed along for a call back.

The company then looks at the job, gives you its own price, does the work and bills you directly. The line never charges you. Companies may pay it a referral fee, and every page of this site says so.

Why washing in Dallas is its own job

Plenty of pressure washing advice is written for other parts of the country. Four things make North Texas different.

Clay under the concrete

Much of the area sits on Blackland Prairie clay, which shrinks and swells as it dries and wets. Driveway slabs crack and tilt, and a wand held too close at a raised edge can chip what is already weak.

Pollen most of the year

Children's Health lists cedar in winter, tree pollen from February to June, grass into September and ragweed into November. Add mold, which peaks in humid late summer, and north walls stay green.

Heat that dries soap on walls

The first 100 degree day at DFW comes on July 1 on average, and the last on August 27. Cleaner that dries on hot brick or siding can streak, so summer jobs tend to run early in the day.

Rules on where the water goes

Storm drains here run to creeks and lakes without treatment. Dallas, Fort Worth and Frisco all address power washers by name in their city rules, and drought plans can limit outdoor washing.

Fences and decks in the Dallas heat

Wood takes the most careful hand. Softwood such as cedar and pine marks easily, so fence cleaning and deck cleaning call for low pressure and a wide fan tip. HGTV puts softwood at roughly 500 to 600 PSI, far below what a concrete job uses.

If a contractor plans to use the same setting on your cedar fence as on your driveway, that is your cue to ask why.

What to ask before you say yes

  • Can I see a certificate of insurance?
  • What pressure and tip will you use on each surface?
  • If you use soap, how will you keep it out of the storm drain?
  • Is the price for the whole job, and is it in writing?
  • Is my home old enough that lead paint is a concern?

Texas does not license power washing, so these questions do the job a license number would do in other trades. Read how the line works for what happens after you call.

Common questions

Does Dallas Power Washing Pro do the washing?

No. It is a free phone line and this website. It owns no equipment and does no cleaning. Your call is transferred to an independent local power washing company, which inspects the job, quotes it, does the work and bills you. Companies may pay the line a referral fee.

How much does pressure washing cost in Dallas?

The price comes from the company you talk to, never from the line. As a starting point, Angi publishes an average of $293 for pressure washing a house in Dallas, with most projects between $174 and $418. Size, stories, surface and stains all move a real quote. The Dallas cost guide compares several published ranges.

Can I wash my driveway during Dallas water restrictions?

The twice-weekly schedule in Dallas is about lawn watering. Pavement washing is covered by the drought plan instead, which at Stage 3 bans hosing paved areas and buildings unless there is a variance and a professional service with high efficiency equipment does the work. Ask Dallas Water Utilities what stage applies on the day you plan to wash.

Is it legal for wash water to run into a Dallas storm drain?

Plain water can be, within limits. Dallas city code gives a defense for water used on driveways, sidewalks and parking lots when it holds no soap, degreaser or similar cleaner. Mobile power washing or pavement washdown with a harmful quantity of those products is prohibited. Soapy water should be collected, not sent to the street.

What cities does the line take calls from?

The Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex only. That includes Dallas, Fort Worth, Arlington, Plano, Frisco, McKinney, Denton, Carrollton, Flower Mound, Addison, Southlake, Keller, Grapevine and nearby communities. The service areas page has the full list.
